**Yes, the cable can be the bottleneck.** Charging runs at the lowest limit among the charger, the device, and the cable. A certified cable doesn't add capability to a charger or device ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector)).

## What the ratings mean
- **60W:** 20V at 3A ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector)). It's fine for phones, tablets, and many small laptops.
- **100W:** 20V at 5A, and the cable needs an e-marker chip. Without one, a charger won't offer more than 60W.
- **240W (EPR):** 48V at 5A. These cables must have an e-marker ([UL Solutions](https://www.ul.com/insights/240w-usb-c-cable-performance-testing-and-safety-considerations)). The higher voltage steps are 28V for 140W, 36V for 180W, and 48V for 240W ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/usb-charger-pd)).

**A labeling catch:** USB-IF stopped certifying 100W USB-C cables on December 22, 2021, and now only certifies 60W and 240W ([UL Solutions](https://www.ul.com/insights/240w-usb-c-cable-performance-testing-and-safety-considerations)). Plenty of 100W cables are still sold and work fine, but they're no longer a certified category. Look for the official 60W or 240W logo if you want a certified cable.

## Which one do you need?
- **Device draws 60W or less:** a 60W cable is enough.
- **Device draws 65–100W:** use a 5A e-marked cable (100W or 240W).
- **Device draws more than 100W:** you need a 240W cable, plus a charger and device that both support it.
- A faster cable won't charge a device faster than its own limit, and a 240W cable on a 65W charger still gives 65W.

## One example if you need 100W
The [Baseus USB-C to USB-C Cable, 100W](https://dealectric.com/baseus-usb-c-cable-100w) is e-marked at 5A and costs $9.99 for 1 m ($12.99 for 2 m, $16.99 for 3 m). The listing notes these limits:
- It is not rated for 140W or 240W.
- Data is USB 2.0 only (480 Mbps), with no video output.
- Baseus says it isn't supported for iPad Pro charging.

That page is a Dealectric affiliate listing, so it may earn them a commission. It's one option, not the only one.

If you tell me your charger and device (for example, a 65W laptop), I can say which cable rating you actually need.
